name: Gautam Biswas
title: Cornelius Vanderbilt Professor of Engineering; Professor of Computer Science; Senior Research Scientist, ISIS
department: Computer Science; Institute for Convergent Software Integrated Systems
fitReason: The MACS research program develops deep RL, neural disturbance estimation and safety analysis for autonomous vehicles, with executed UAV transfer and current safe continual-learning methods.

physicalEvidence.summary: DX 2024 primary paper reports five actual flights at Fort Devens, Massachusetts, using the vehicle labeled DJI S100 octocopter in the paper. A ground-station PPO controller adjusts X/Y velocity references every 0.5 seconds using an LSTM disturbance estimate; ArduPilot performs low-level control. This is executed learned supervision, separate from the simulated Tarot T-18 and from neural models used afterward to analyze flight data. MIT Lincoln Laboratory flight support is acknowledged, so current Vanderbilt-local access is not established. The directed-group connection is independently supported by Biswas’s staff/student roster. April 2026 SafeEWC uses MuJoCo and Continual World simulation, not fresh robot execution.

shortVisit.summary: No explicit current external-master short-visit invitation found on the official faculty/home/lab pages. MACS co-lead Marcos Quiñones-Grueiro records 2025–2026 graduate visitors, including one- and three-month stays, but these are past group-level precedents without a confirmed master category or open offer from Biswas.
